meta.title: Cincinnati Music Hall
meta.summary: One grand building, so many kinds of sound. I’ll take you beyond the facade to see how Cincinnati keeps Music Hall alive.

sourceRefs.label: Cincinnati Arts Association · About Music Hall

blocks.text: Let me start with Cincinnati Music Hall: it dates to 1878, and its Elm Street façade still makes me want to stop and look up. The hall first served as a convention center as well as a performance space; industrial exhibitions, public events, and concerts all belong to its history. This grand building has always needed people gathering inside, not only admiring it from the street.

Today it is home to the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra, Pops Orchestra, Opera, Ballet, and May Festival, among others. Its long program has also included sports, conventions, and contemporary musicians. I like that range: a cultural landmark isn't frozen in its opening year. If you're planning a visit, look for a performance that draws you in and check the current calendar. The room changes with the people onstage and in the seats. I’d keep time to admire the facade before a performance. A little anticipation is part of the evening—especially with good company. ♡
